annotations.title: You thought euil.
annotations.text: ◦ This plaine diſtinction sheweth, that ſinne is wholly of the ſinner; and that God hath no part therin, but turneth it to good. For thoſe things which Ioſephs brethren did againſt him, were occaſions of his aduancement in Ægypt, through the omnipotent wiſdome of God. VVhoſe propertie is, out of euerie euil to draw good. S. Chriſoſt. ho. 67. in Gen. S. Aug. Enchirid. c. 11. & li. 14. c. 27. de ciuit.

notes.text: Mans wil, not God the cause of sinne.

annotations.title: Carie my bones with you.
annotations.text: For the ſame reaſons Ioſeph would be finally buried in Chanaan, for which Iacob deſired to be there buried (chap. 47.) but Ioſeph would not preſently be caried thither, <mn>◦</mn>leſt it might haue geuen offence to the Ægyptians; or at leaſt haue diminished their fauoure towardes his brethren: and withal he would confirme his brethren in their hope of returning, ſeing he was content, that his bodie should expect in Ægypt, til the whole Nation ſhould returne into Chanaan.

notes.text: Ioseph, for his brethrés sake, differred his desired burial in Chanaan.
